decisions.reason: As a wholesaler, the cost of leaving a newly launched finisher with its own page in the portfolio is low, and with no clear negative signal yet the option value of waiting still exceeds the case for withdrawal.
The home-page placement and named Germany premiere suggest active commercial backing, so management would likely keep the product while early market uncertainty resolves.
Although there is no reported sales proof yet, a dedicated product page indicates a real launch and the low ongoing cost of offering a niche module supports keeping the option open.
This B2 multifinisher received prominent home-page launch treatment with a dated announcement, indicating strategic importance and too little negative evidence to justify abandonment.
The hybrid saddle stitcher appears to be an exploratory portfolio extension, and absent clear failure management would likely continue offering it because the cost of waiting is modest.
The cited installation at a customer provides an early adoption signal, so despite being only briefly mentioned on the site the product still looks worth keeping on the market.
